worlds.title: Six worlds, one at a time
worlds.caption: The number of agents alive after every game in the worlds with seeds 1 to 6, each in a chart of its own and all on the same scale (0 to 25,000 agents, iterations 0 to 1,500). Each line has one point per iteration.
worlds.recipe:
**Runs.** `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s006`, six of the 30 baseline runs (their settings are listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)).

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).

1. Take the rows with `phase` = 2.
2. Plot `nodes` against `iteration`, one point per iteration, joined.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py life`.

agents.title: Agents alive, 30 worlds
agents.caption: The line is the median of the worlds at each iteration, the darker band holds the middle half of them (from the 25th to the 75th percentile) and the paler band nine in ten (5th to 95th). All 30 live to the end.
agents.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).

1. Take every run's rows with `phase` = 2 and the statistic `nodes`.
2. Cut the 1,500 iterations into 600 stretches of 2.5 and take each world's mean in each stretch.
3. In each stretch, take the median, the 25th and 75th and the 5th and 95th percentiles of those means over the worlds that still have a value there (a world that died has none after its death).

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py life`.

early-late.title: Each world early and late
early-late.caption: One line per world, from its mean number of agents over iterations 100–200 (left) to its mean over iterations 1,300–1,499 (right). Green: the late mean is more than 1.2 times the early one; red: less than 0.8 times; grey: in between. The thick blue line joins the medians of the 30 worlds.
early-late.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).

1. For each run that reached iteration 1,500, take the rows with `phase` = 2.
2. Average `nodes` over the rows with 100 ≤ `iteration` ≤ 200, and again over 1,300 ≤ `iteration` ≤ 1,499.
3. Draw one line from the first mean to the second; colour it by their ratio.
4. Join the two medians over the 30 runs.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py life`.

connections.caption: The number of connections after every game. The line is the median of the worlds at each iteration, the darker band holds the middle half of them (from the 25th to the 75th percentile) and the paler band nine in ten (5th to 95th).
